correctness.rationale: Subtracting the equal-weight ensemble mean from each particle removes the common mean term and yields a scalar linear residual SDE with kernel ((T-t)/(T-s))^alpha. At each fixed t the kernel integrals are iid centered Gaussians with variance v_alpha(t), so the entire residual vector is exactly sigma sqrt(v_alpha(t)) times an iid Gaussian sample centered by its empirical mean. The maximum differs from the ordinary absolute-Gaussian maximum by at most |bar Z_n|; since sqrt(log n)|bar Z_n| tends to zero, both first-order scaling and the 1/b_n Gumbel refinement transfer. Direct integration gives the three alpha regimes and hence the exact condition v_alpha(t_n) log n -> 0 for simultaneous pinning, with the stated critical windows. A fresh analytic/numeric check confirmed positivity and the closed-form regimes, while the packaged verifier separately checks quadrature and tail normalization.

value.rationale: The model source explicitly identifies convergence speed as an open issue. Uniform pinning of every particle when the ensemble size grows is a natural stronger question than pointwise finite-n pinning, and the theorem supplies sharp transition scales plus a second-order Gumbel profile. The three alpha regimes expose a genuine phase change at alpha=1/2.

limitations: Equal weights, one segment, no common noise, homogeneous Gaussian idiosyncratic noise and f(t)=alpha/(T-t) only.
